phase_name: Measure the LEAN_NUM_THREADS cap on this toolchain

objectives.description: Create probe.lean: standalone CPU-bound Task probe, no Mathlib/FormalSystem imports
Run probe twice under /usr/bin/time -v (LEAN_NUM_THREADS unset, then =1), capture CPU-percent
Write probe-results.md with both commands, measurements, nproc, lean --version

objectives.note: Verdict: inconclusive. Pure Task.spawn never parallelized on this toolchain regardless of LEAN_NUM_THREADS (confirmed via /proc thread polling); switched to IO.asTask which does achieve genuine concurrency, but the official measurement (48-way flat fan-out) showed no capping effect either direction, most plausibly because that task shape triggers Lean's documented soft-limit-exceeded-to-avoid-deadlock behavior rather than genuinely refuting the mechanism. A Lake maintainer (Mac Malone, leanprover-community Zulip) directly vouches for LEAN_NUM_THREADS as the sanctioned fix for this class of OOM. Not a blocker per plan's own contingency.

approaches_tried.approach: Pure Task.spawn on a CPU-bound closure, including Task.Priority.dedicated
approaches_tried.reason: Never observed more than 1 thread in Running state via /proc/<pid>/task polling on a compiled build, regardless of LEAN_NUM_THREADS setting -- this toolchain's pure Task.spawn does not appear to use the worker pool for scheduling.

deviations.description: Probe mechanism: plan said "IO.asTask or Task.spawn"
deviations.reason: Task.spawn tried first and found non-functional for concurrency on this toolchain (confirmed via /proc thread-state polling); switched to IO.asTask, the plan's other explicitly named alternative, which does achieve genuine multi-thread concurrency.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- used IO.asTask instead of Task.spawn, both named by the plan; Task.spawn confirmed non-functional for concurrency on this toolchain)*
